chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Other small-label dates with Hodges, Brown and Strayhorn on congas
summary: Jones played piano on Wax and Granz-label sessions with Johnny Hodges, Lawrence Brown, Billy Strayhorn and others.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And I was lucky to have those men to, you know. Then there was another time when I used to -- oh, we were recording another small label, I was playing piano, with Lawrence Brown, Johnny Hodges, Al Hall the bass player, Denzil Best the drummer, and Billy Strayhorn was playing congas.
What were those records, all of them?
Yeah, it was called Wax records. It goes way back awhile, you know?
I never knew Strays played congas.
Yeah, well all he had to do was stay there and keep time with Denzil, you know.
Yeah, but I just never knew he recorded as a conga player.

Yeah. He was playing congas. And I'm playing piano, and it worked quite well. Worked out very good. Then another time I did some things with playing piano with Johnny and Lawrence, with Aaron Bell on bass and Sonny Greer on drums.
That was -- what's the record company that Norman created?
Well, there've been so many. Norgran, Clef, those were his early ones.
And there was a couple of others.
Well this one went to MGM, I think he said.
Started with a V, didn't it?
